task.description: Gate the new one-way-gate test added in this rework. Independently re-run `mix test test/letflow/plugs/iss0736_oidc_live_revocation_test.exs --seed 0` yourself and confirm the real output (do not trust the handoff's claim of 3 passed). Then independently apply a mutant that breaks the one-way-gate specifically -- e.g. change the call-site guard from `role_claims_synced_at == nil` to always-true (always re-sync), or make sync_role_claims_from_token/3 unconditionally reset the marker -- in a throwaway worktree, confirm the new one-way-gate test (and only that one, ideally) fails against the mutant, then revert and verify git status clean. This is the specific security property this whole rework exists to protect, so the mutant must target exactly this, not an arbitrary line. Also independently assess: TEST-DESIGNER reported the full mix letflow.check.test hit a pre-existing `versions_missing = [20260921000001]` migration-state mismatch (130/211 passed) they attributed to being unrelated to their changes -- form your own view (is this plausibly a concurrent-session artifact from a stale test DB, e.g. another process holding a pre-migration tenant_template schema, similar to what ELIXIR-DEV's step-03-elixir-dev-rework1 already encountered and worked around) and flag it clearly for TEST-RUNNER's attention rather than letting it get silently reintroduced as a blocker there.

result.summary: Independently re-ran `mix test test/letflow/plugs/iss0736_oidc_live_revocation_test.exs --seed 0` against the branch as-is (not trusting the prior handoff's claim): real output 'Finished in 4.0 seconds (0.00s async, 4.0s sync)' / 'Result: 3 passed', 0 failures -- confirms all 3 tests (the 2 pre-existing AC1 tests plus the new §2.2 one-way-gate test) genuinely pass. Applied a mutant targeting the one-way-gate specifically, in a throwaway `git worktree` (`../letflow-mutant-check`, detached at the branch's HEAD, deps/_build pointed at the main checkout's via MIX_DEPS_PATH/MIX_BUILD_PATH since a worktree does not share gitignored build artifacts): in `lib/letflow/identity.ex`'s `upsert_by_external_identity/4`, changed the call-site gate `if is_nil(existing.role_claims_synced_at) do` (line 1602, the repeat-login branch the test's 2nd and 3rd requests both go through) to `if true do`, i.e. always re-sync regardless of the marker -- exactly the one-way-gate property REQ-378 §2.2 exists to protect. Re-ran the same targeted file against the mutant: 'Finished in 4.7 seconds (0.00s async, 4.7s sync)' / 'Result: 2/3 passed' / 1 failure -- the new §2.2 one-way-gate test failed (`assert revoked_conn.status == 403` got `200`, at test line 289: the mutant's unconditional re-sync re-inserted the group_members row on the very first post-revocation request, before the one-way-gate's own later assertion at line 294-295 was even reached), while both pre-existing AC1 tests (which never exercise the sync path -- they pre-seed group_members directly) continued to pass unaffected. This is the isolation the acceptance criteria call for: the mutant is caught by, and only by, the test designed to catch it. Reverted via `git checkout -- lib/letflow/identity.ex` inside the worktree, then removed the worktree (`git worktree remove ../letflow-mutant-check --force`); verified clean with `git status --porcelain lib/ test/` in the main checkout, which returned no output (empty), confirming no residue from the probe. Re-confirmed the targeted test file was untouched and still green throughout (no edits were made to test/ at any point in this validation). Also assessed the `versions_missing = [20260921000001]` full-suite failure TEST-DESIGNER flagged: `20260921000001_add_role_claims_synced_at_to_users.exs` is exactly the migration this rework's ELIXIR-DEV step added (confirmed via `lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex:561`'s manifest entry), and that same ELIXIR-DEV rework1 handoff (`handoffs/WF03-ISS0736-20260921/step-03-elixir-dev-rework1.json`) independently documents hitting the identical mechanism first-hand during its own targeted run: 'initially collided with a concurrent, still-running sibling mix test process ... holding a stale tenant_template schema built before this migration existed ... re-ran against an isolated MIX_TEST_PARTITION=_elixirdev_iss0736 database ... to avoid racing that sibling session.' A stale, pre-20260921000001 tenant_template schema cached by a concurrent process is exactly what would produce `versions_missing = [20260921000001]` when `TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1` provisions from it across many unrelated full-suite files. This is plausible and consistent with documented precedent on this same branch, not merely TEST-DESIGNER's unverified say-so -- but it is a live-environment/concurrent-session state issue, not something this gate step can independently reproduce or rule out further (no access to what else was running on the machine at TEST-DESIGNER's run time). Flagging clearly, as instructed, rather than letting it resurface silently: TEST-RUNNER's full-suite gate should first re-run `mix letflow.check.test` in isolation (no concurrent `mix test`/`mix ecto` process against the same default test DB, per the same `MIX_TEST_PARTITION` workaround ELIXIR-DEV already used) before treating 130/211 as a real regression from this branch's changes.
